personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: I want to ship fast, and a second approval slows me, but I choose when to ask for it.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: I don't master the technical harness, so one named engineer checking it lets me push quick wins with less worry.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: It keeps the teams' code cohesive, but I only look at the board, so a request could sit with me.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: A person reads the plan before agents write slop, and only that person can approve it.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: Being able to change the data shape before code exists is useful, if the grill stays short and isn't fluff.

objection.text: I mostly just look at the board. If PMs can send me a long grilling session whenever they like, those requests will sit there, and nothing tells the PM that their PRD is stuck on me.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: Asked last, and only if I want it, so my normal brainstorm stays the same. Once I ask, I wait.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: The product choices stay mine, and the review covers coding only, so my customer decisions aren't reopened.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: An email and my Waiting section are enough, and the agent asks only what the plan leaves open.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: Nobody can skip it once requested, and the database refuses the product approval without it.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: Reading the code before asking is right. I'll judge it by whether the questions are worth answering.

personas.name: Paul - Product Manager
personas.reaction: The note says it plainly: I can ask one engineer, and the build then waits for both approvals. I choose when, and that wait is the price.

personas.name: Irisa
personas.reaction: A named engineer approves the plan on the PRD's page, so I can push quick wins with less worry about the technical side.

personas.name: Lead Engineer
personas.reaction: I'm asked by name and it shows in Waiting, which suits me. Email now being on by default means more mail unless I switch it off.

personas.name: F-E Developer
personas.reaction: Two seals and a Stage line naming who it waits on are clear, and the page reads the product approval only. I'd still want to see it in a browser.

personas.name: B-E DEv
personas.reaction: The database refuses the product approval without the tech one, which I trust. The review's who-are-you check runs only in the terminal, though giving the approval does not.
